findings.title: Numeric IPv4 notation bypasses the metadata SSRF block
findings.problem: InstanceConfig(url="http://2852039166", enabled=True) succeeds. The helper at triggarr/web/validation.py:150-173 treats this numeric host as an arbitrary hostname after ipaddress rejects it. Verified that HTTPX preserves the host and socket.getaddrinfo with AI_NUMERICHOST resolves it to 169.254.169.254 without DNS. Startup passes the accepted URL into the client at triggarr/startup.py:153-160, permitting requests to the metadata address this new check explicitly intends to block. This is a concrete bypass, independent of the documented DNS-rebinding exception.

members.title: Domain config model now depends on the web package, making triggarr.models and triggarr.web depend on each other
members.problem: The validator `InstanceConfig.validate_url_ssrf` imports `triggarr.web.validation.validate_arr_url_config`. That makes the models layer depend on the web/UI layer. The opposite direction already exists: `triggarr/web/routes.py:47-48` imports `InstanceConfig`/`Settings` from `triggarr.models.config`. Both edges are in view, so the two packages now depend on each other. This is not a runtime import cycle: `triggarr/web/validation.py` imports only stdlib (`ipaddress`, `re`, `urllib.parse`) and `triggarr/web/__init__.py` is empty. That is also why the function-local import is not needed to break a cycle. There is a precedent that lowers the severity: `triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532,538` already imports from `triggarr.web.routes` inside functions, so lower layers reaching into `web` is not unheard of in this codebase.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: With config schema validation living in the web package, a later change to triggarr/web/validation.py (for example, importing routes, templates or FastAPI helpers) could create a real import cycle at config load. Startup would then fail before any instance runs. The function-local import also hides that dependency from readers and from import-graph tooling.
members.fix_hint: Move the stdlib-only URL/SSRF validators (validate_arr_url, validate_arr_url_config, BLOCKED_HOSTS, _BLOCKED_NETWORKS) into a neutral module such as triggarr/models/url_validation.py or triggarr/net_validation.py. Have both web.routes and models.config import that module at the top level, and keep web.validation re-exporting the validators so existing imports keep working.
members.current_code:
from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config

        ok, err = validate_arr_url_config(v)

members.title: A failed URL check now produces an uncaught startup traceback instead of a friendly config error
members.problem: The ensure_config docstring (triggarr/config.py:343-345) treats pydantic.ValidationError as a 'schema bug' and lets it propagate uncaught. This validator is a new way for ordinary user config to trigger that path. A bad scheme, a metadata host or a link-local address is a user-data error, not a schema bug, but the user gets a raw Pydantic traceback, unlike the friendly _log_corrupt_config_and_exit path for TOML errors. The existing apikey validator already had this behavior, so it is partly pre-existing. pending: check whether the startup logs give a usable message naming the instance and field.
members.why_it_matters: A homelab user who hits the new rejection after upgrading sees a crash loop with a traceback and no restore hint.
members.fix_hint: Catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and log a friendly error naming the instance and field, then sys.exit(1)

members.title: Pre-existing gaps in the shared SSRF check: trailing-dot metadata hostname, decimal or short IPv4 forms, plain-IPv4 100.64/10
members.problem: This diff only tightens a control: config loading previously had no SSRF check. The helper it calls compares hostnames by exact string against BLOCKED_HOSTS (validation.py:18), so 'http://metadata.google.internal./' and non-dotted-quad IPv4 forms such as 'http://2852039166/' get past it. ipaddress.ip_address raises ValueError on those strings, which the code treats as a DNS name. The plain-IPv4 _BLOCKED_NETWORKS (100.64/10) check is only applied to IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses. The web-form validator validate_arr_url accepted the same inputs before this diff, so these are pre-existing gaps, not regressions. pending: a resolver test showing httpx sends 2852039166 or a trailing-dot host to 169.254.169.254.
source_window: is still rejected at startup (intended hardening per D-01/D-02).
Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: The new load-time check gives less protection than its docstring suggests for cloud-metadata targets.
members.fix_hint: Strip a trailing dot before the BLOCKED_HOSTS lookup; optionally normalize numeric host forms with socket.inet_aton

findings.title: New URL validator turns previously-loadable configs into an uncaught ValidationError crash at startup
findings.problem: The validator runs for every instance, including disabled ones, so any url in triggarr.toml without an http/https scheme now raises at load time. Examples: a hand-edited `url = "radarr:7878"` (urlparse reads the scheme as 'radarr'), `"192.168.1.10:7878"` (empty scheme), or a v2.2-migrated value saved before validate_arr_url existed. Before this change these loaded fine, and a disabled instance with one was harmless. ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:370-373) catches only TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, and its docstring treats a ValidationError as a 'schema bug' that propagates uncaught. startup.py:192 has no handler either. The daemon now dies with a raw pydantic traceback instead of the friendly log-and-exit used for corrupt TOML, which can put a Docker container into a restart loop. pending: confirm whether scheme-less or hand-edited URLs are a supported config shape. The web UI save path already rejects them (routes.py:561), but hand-edited TOML and old migrated configs bypass it.
findings.fix_hint: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and log a friendly path-only error naming the offending instance/field, then sys.exit(1); optionally skip the check for disabled instances
findings.why_it_matters: After upgrading, users with a legacy or hand-edited URL on even a disabled instance get a crash-looping container and a raw traceback instead of a clear error.

needs_verification.consequence: pydantic.ValidationError propagates uncaught from ensure_config, so the daemon exits with a traceback at every start (Docker restart loop) where before the upgrade it started normally

findings.title: New url validator can stop startup for hand-edited TOML URLs that used to load, such as http://0.0.0.0:7878
findings.problem: validate_url_ssrf now runs validate_arr_url_config on every InstanceConfig.url, including disabled instances. That function rejects unspecified, link-local and multicast IP literals (triggarr/web/validation.py:153) and any URL without an http(s) scheme. Before this diff, a hand-edited triggarr.toml with url = "http://0.0.0.0:7878" or "http://[::]:8989" loaded fine. Connecting to 0.0.0.0 reaches the local host on Linux and macOS, so that URL could have been working. Now load_settings (triggarr/config.py:227) raises pydantic.ValidationError. ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:371) only catches TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, so the process exits with a raw traceback and a Docker restart policy keeps restarting it. The web settings form already rejected these values (routes.py:561 uses the stricter validate_arr_url), so only hand-edited configs are affected. pending: confirm whether 0.0.0.0 or [::] same-host URLs (or IPv6 link-local with a zone id) are supported config values.
findings.fix_hint: Decide whether 0.0.0.0/[::] count as same-host values like 127.0.0.1; either way, catch ValidationError in ensure_config and log a clear error naming the field instead of a traceback
findings.why_it_matters: An existing install with such a URL, even on a disabled instance, stops starting after upgrade and gives no friendly error.
